batchName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: The Severans and the Crisis of the Third Century (AD 193-284)

questions.question: What was the Tetrarchy, set up in 293?
options: A tax on four kinds of goods
questions.explanation: The Tetrarchy was a team of four co-emperors created by a soldier-emperor who seized power in 284. Its creation marked the end of the crisis.
questions.sourceQuote: The crisis ended with Diocletian, a soldier-emperor who seized power in 284 and in 293 set up the Tetrarchy, a team of four co-emperors.

questions.question: In which city was Septimius Severus, founder of the Severan dynasty, born?
questions.explanation: Severus was born in 145 at Leptis Magna, a rich port on the coast of modern Libya. His family had Libyan, Punic and Italian roots.
questions.sourceQuote: Severus was born in 145 at Leptis Magna, a rich port on the coast of modern Libya.

questions.question: Who was behind the murder of Caracalla in 217?
questions.explanation: Caracalla's own praetorian prefect, commander of the emperor's elite bodyguard, organised his murder. Under the Severans this post became a powerful and dangerous office.
questions.sourceQuote: The man behind Caracalla's murder in 217 was his praetorian prefect (*praefectus praetorio*), commander of the Praetorian Guard (*cohortes praetoriae*), the emperor's elite bodyguard.

questions.question: The teenage emperor remembered as Elagabalus was a priest of which deity?
questions.explanation: He was a 14-year-old priest of the Syrian sun god Elagabal and is remembered by his god's name, as Elagabalus. In 220 he even placed his god above Jupiter.
questions.sourceQuote: The first, a 14-year-old priest of the Syrian sun god Elagabal, is remembered by his god's name, as Elagabalus.

questions.question: Which frontier fortification did Septimius Severus rebuild during his British campaigns?
questions.explanation: Severus campaigned in Britain from 208 to 210 and rebuilt Hadrian's Wall. Before that he had beaten the Parthians in the east.
questions.sourceQuote: Severus then beat the Parthians, the rulers of Persia and Mesopotamia, and from 208 to 210 he campaigned in Britain and rebuilt Hadrian's Wall.

questions.question: By the end of the third century, what had become of the denarius, Rome's standard coin?
options: It was worth twice as much
It was made of pure gold
It was replaced by Persian coins
questions.explanation: Emperors kept adding bronze and copper to the coin, so prices spiralled and the denarius became nearly worthless. The debasement began with Septimius Severus.
questions.sourceQuote: Prices spiralled, and by the century's end the denarius was nearly worthless.

questions.question: What were the 'barracks emperors'?
options: Men raised by soldiers without political experience or noble birth
Generals who refused the throne out of loyalty
Senators who governed from military camps
Emperors who built new forts along the frontiers
questions.explanation: Barracks emperors were raised by soldiers and had no political experience, noble ancestors or hereditary claim. The first was a legion commander of peasant origin.
questions.sourceQuote: The army's new emperor, Maximinus Thrax, a legion commander of peasant origin, was the first of the barracks emperors: men raised by soldiers without political experience, noble ancestors or hereditary claim.

questions.question: What did Caracalla grant to every free person in the Roman Empire?
questions.explanation: Caracalla extended Roman citizenship to every free person in the empire, for reasons that are still unclear. His great public baths in Rome also still stand.
questions.sourceQuote: For reasons still unclear, he granted Roman citizenship (*civitas*) to every free person in the empire.

questions.question: How did Septimius Severus die in 211?
options: Killed in battle against the Parthians
Poisoned by his son in Rome
Of natural causes while in Britain
questions.explanation: He died of natural causes in Britain in 211, after campaigning there and rebuilding Hadrian’s Wall.
questions.sourceQuote: He died of natural causes in Britain in 211.

questions.question: By 268, Gaul, Britain and briefly Spain had formed which breakaway state?
questions.explanation: The Gallic Empire was one of three pieces the Roman Empire had split into by 268. In the east, Palmyra held power.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaul, Britain and briefly Spain formed a breakaway Gallic Empire.
